tasks.short: Direct and supervise workers on site.

steps.what: Direct and supervise construction workers on site.
Note an instruction that changes the day's work.

tasks.design: Today's work list comes from the issued schedule in {PROJECT}. The construction manager directs and supervises the workers on site. A note is written only when an instruction changes the day. The list does not supervise anyone and does not score a worker. The manager stays on the site for this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: The day's order was shouted from memory, and a change was lost by the afternoon.
tasks.enabler_now: An issued schedule can show today's activities. Standing with the crew cannot be shown.
tasks.still_hard: Weather at 7 a.m., a missing gang, and work that is unsafe to start.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sees the person, the edge, and whether the instruction was understood.
tasks.altitude: Nothing important moves. The list is ready at the start of the day. Direction and supervision stay on the site with the manager.

reach.task: Direct a shift in the building, in person, from a list of what is due.
reach.learn: The list is not the supervision. This manager still stands with the crew.

evidence.claim: A schedule can list today's activities. It cannot direct a person on a scaffold.

The job digest says staff evaluation and behaviour scoring are high-risk, and rosters that monitor staff need works-council consent. This task adds no score and no roster. The manager supervises in person.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Activity id and planned day, produced by the issued schedule. The note does not store a rating of a named worker. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read today's activities from the existing plan before a new board.
unknowns: How the site records a verbal stop-work instruction today.
Whether a works council already limits site monitoring.
research_questions: Is the issued schedule trusted at the morning start?
What share of instructions change the day?

already_counted.description: The manager still supervises on site.
The manager still notes a changed instruction.

incremental.description: No new tool is added for supervision. The manager only checks that today's list still matches the issued schedule.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Supervision is the task and stays on site. The only saving is having today's list ready, and it vanishes when the issued schedule is already wrong at dawn.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine labour hours before any dispatch.

steps.what: Sum hours by trade from the quantities.
Determine labor requirements for dispatching workers.
Record the hours by trade, not named people.

tasks.design: Quantities and output rates in {PROJECT} sum to hours by trade. The construction manager determines the labour requirement for the site, including what dispatching workers will later need, and records hours by trade. The table does not name a person and does not dispatch anyone. A trade with no output rate is left for the manager to set.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hours were guessed from the last job, and the guess was treated as a crew list.
tasks.enabler_now: A quantity and a rate can produce hours. Choosing the requirement, and refusing to name people, stays the manager.
tasks.still_hard: Rates that do not fit this building, and a site that needs a named chargehand the table must not pick.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows the access, the overtime already worked, and which trade is actually short.
tasks.altitude: The arithmetic of hours is ready before the conversation. The manager still sets the requirement. Named dispatch is not this task and does not start here.

reach.task: Turn a volume into hours before anyone is assigned to a shift.
reach.learn: Hours are not a roster. This manager does not assign named workers.

evidence.claim: A quantity times a rate can show hours by trade. It cannot choose a person.

The job digest says rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk under the EU AI Act, staff decisions need a person under GDPR article 22, and rosters need works-council consent. This task stops at hours by trade. It does not dispatch named workers.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Trade, quantity, and output rate, produced by the quantity takeoff and the rate table. The signed requirement has no person-name field. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing quantity and rate tables before a new labour tool.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
Dispatch of named people is out of scope. A later roster, if any, needs its own works-council consent.
unknowns: Whether dispatch is done by this manager or by a supervisor.
research_questions: Are output rates written for this building type?
Does any current sheet already list named people against these hours?

already_counted.description: The manager still determines the requirement.
The manager still signs the hours by trade.

incremental.description: The manager updates an output rate when the method changes.

approvals.approved_version: trade ids and the hours shown to the manager

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Setting the requirement stays with the manager. Saving is the hour sum, and it shrinks when output rates are missing and the manager still builds the table.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer on site problems with the parties.

steps.what: List open construction complaints and procedure questions.
Confer with owners and contractors on the problems.
Note which problem was resolved and which was not.

tasks.design: Open complaints and procedure questions are listed from {PROJECT} before the meeting. The construction manager confers with owners, contractors, and design professionals and resolves what can be resolved in the room. The list does not decide the problem. A note records only what was actually agreed. Design staff and supervisors are in that conversation, not in a score.
tasks.previous_blocker: The meeting started from memory, and an agreement was later denied because nobody wrote the sentence down.
tasks.enabler_now: Open items can be listed. The conference itself is the work.
tasks.still_hard: A problem that is really a claim, a personality, or a design that is not finished.
tasks.human_edge: The manager hears what the owner will actually accept, which a list cannot hear.
tasks.altitude: The meeting starts from a list. The conferring and the resolution stay with the manager. The week does not lose this conversation.

reach.task: Hold the difficult meeting and write only what was agreed.
reach.learn: An agenda is not the agreement. This manager still sits in the room.

evidence.claim: A project log can list open items. It cannot hold the meeting.
Resolving a complaint can change money or time. The manager does that in the room. No recording of the meeting is added, because the job digest says staff monitoring needs works-council consent.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Item id, party, and open status, produced by the project log. The resolution sentence is written by the manager after the meeting, not generated before it. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing issue log before a new complaints tool.
unknowns: Which parties must be in the room.
Whether any agreement needs a formal instruction to count.
research_questions: What share of problems are already on the log?
How often is an oral agreement later disputed?

already_counted.description: The manager still confers with the parties.
The manager still writes what was resolved.

incremental.description: The manager adds a problem type when a new kind of complaint appears.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The meeting is almost the whole task. Saving is the list of open items, and it shrinks when the real problems are not on the log yet.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Mark clauses that differ from the standard set.

loop.input: the draft and the standard clause ids
loop.output: a list of clauses that differ
loop.check: each difference cites a standard clause id
loop.stop: stop when the draft has no clause ids
loop.why_not_simpler: contract language is free text, so a cell match is not enough

steps.what: Negotiate revisions with suppliers or subcontractors.

tasks.design: The draft contract in {CLM} is compared with the standard clauses, and each difference is listed. The construction manager negotiates revisions with architects, consultants, clients, suppliers, or subcontractors, then signs the contractual agreement. The deviation list does not concede a clause. A draft with no clause ids is read by the manager instead.
tasks.previous_blocker: The manager read the whole subcontract the night before the meeting and still missed a changed indemnity.
tasks.enabler_now: Clause ids can show a difference. Giving the point away is still a negotiation.
tasks.still_hard: A counterparty draft that uses no ids, and a commercial trade that is not in the legal text yet.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which clause this subcontractor will fight, and which difference is actually dangerous.
tasks.altitude: Differences are visible before the meeting. The negotiation and the signature stay with the manager.

reach.role: Brownfield Redevelopment Specialists and Site Managers
reach.task: Negotiate a constraint that is commercial as well as technical.
reach.learn: A marked clause is not a concession. This manager still negotiates.

evidence.claim: A clause table can mark text that differs from a standard id. It cannot decide the commercial trade.
Signing a contract is a legal act of the manager. The job digest says a model may mark deviations and a person decides. This signature is that decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Clause id in the draft and in the standard set, produced by the contract file. No clause id means the comparison stops. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing contract file before a new comparison tool.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
unknowns: Who has authority to sign which contract value.
Whether the client imposes a form with no clause ids.
research_questions: Do subcontract forms carry clause ids?
Which clauses are negotiated on every job?

already_counted.description: The manager still negotiates the revision.
The manager still signs the agreement.

incremental.description: The manager updates a standard clause when the company form changes.

approvals.approved_version: contract id and the revised text shown to the manager

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Negotiation is most of the task. Saving is the deviation list, and it shrinks when drafts have no clause ids and the manager still reads every line.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager still supervises the crew, still takes the hard meeting, and still negotiates the contract. An hours-by-trade total can be prepared first.
reach: Loss prevention managers investigate what happened on site, and this job learns supervision is not a score of the worker.
Brownfield redevelopment specialists negotiate access and land constraints, and this job learns a clause table is not the negotiation.
skills_to_grow: State labour as hours by trade, and refuse a list of named people ranked by speed.
Mark a contract clause that differs from the standard set before the negotiation starts.
role.ambitious_version: A clause that differs from the standard set is on the table before the meeting, and the negotiation still belongs to the manager.
